subject: Sex as individual covariate in stratified population model

messages.author: d696738754c1eda3
messages.subject: Sex as individual covariate in stratified population model
parts:
Hi all

I have a dataset on leopards that consists of six session from six different camera trap arrays. 
I have been using ´secr´ v. 3.2.0 on my dataset to estimate density, detection and the scale parameter with various covariates successfully, but when I try to run a model using sex as a individual covariate on sigma I get this error:

> md7 <- secr.fit(capthist = 'leo', model=list(D~dRes_st, g0~dRiv_st, sigma~Sex),
+                 buffer=buffer1, mask=leoudzmask)
Checking data 
Preparing detection design matrices 
Error in secr.design.MS(capthist, model, timecov, sessioncov, groups,  : 
  seems you are trying to use individual covariates  in a full-likelihood model

As an alternative I tried to model sex as a group and first got an error I don't know how to fix:
> md7 <- secr.fit(capthist = 'leo', model=list(D~dRes_st, g0~dRiv_st, sigma~session),
+                 buffer=buffer1, mask=leoudzmask, groups = "Sex", CL = FALSE)
Checking data 
Preparing detection design matrices 
Preparing density design matrix 
Error in `[<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, , i, value = c(-0.821609015954664,  : 
  replacement has 11070 rows, data has 22140

Then I tried running the same model except CL = TRUE but got this warning.
> md7 <- secr.fit(capthist = 'leo', model=list(D~dRes_st, g0~dRiv_st, sigma~session),
+                 buffer=buffer1, mask=leoudzmask, groups = "Sex", CL = TRUE)
Warning message:
In secr.fit(capthist = "leo", model = list(D ~ dRes_st, g0 ~ dRiv_st,  :
  groups not valid with CL; groups ignored

Does anybody know if it is possible to use sex as an individual covariate in a multi-session/stratified population model in ´secr´ 3.2.0?

Any advice would be greatly appreciated!

Best regards

Rasmus

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Sex as individual covariate in stratified population model
parts:
Yes. These all work:
library(secr)
msk <- make.mask(traps(ovenCH[[1]]), nx = 32, buffer = 300, type = 'trapbuffer')
fit1 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, model = list(g0~Sex, sigma~Sex), CL = TRUE, mask = msk)
fit2 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, model = list(D~g, g0~g, sigma~g), groups = 'Sex', mask = msk)
fit3 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, model = list(g0~h2, sigma~h2), hcov = 'Sex', mask = msk)

Your first option is wrong for the reason in the error message; it might have worked with CL = TRUE. The second option does not include a sex (group) effect in the model - use 'g' for this as in fit2 above (I admit the code should behave better, and I'll look at that). Your third option is wrong for the reason in the error message: groups are not used in CL = TRUE models (though they may be defined post hoc in derived.secr).

Murray

Hi,

Thanks a lot for your swift reply, Jo. Adding CL=FALSE does seem to solve the problem of the models all being interpreted as being the same (see output below), but unfortunately it introduces another problem. Fitting conditional likelihood models (CL=TRUE) was necessary so that we could model the influence of continuous covariates on density. The models with continuous covariates fail to fit when using CL=FALSE. We could bin the continuous variables into discrete bands (e.g. low, medium, high, etc) to make this work using CL=FALSE, but this would waste some of the information, and deciding where to draw the boundaries between bands could be a bit subjective. 

Before we resort to that, is there anything else that we can do to model density using continuous covariates without all the models being interpreted as the same?

Thanks a lot,

Sam

fredag den 19. april 2019 kl. 11.26.47 UTC+2 skrev Murray Efford:
Yes. These all work:
library(secr)
msk <- make.mask(traps(ovenCH[[1]]), nx = 32, buffer = 300, type = 'trapbuffer')
fit1 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, model = list(g0~Sex, sigma~Sex), CL = TRUE, mask = msk)
fit2 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, model = list(D~g, g0~g, sigma~g), groups = 'Sex', mask = msk)
fit3 <- secr.fit(ovenCH, model = list(g0~h2, sigma~h2), hcov = 'Sex', mask = msk)

Your first option is wrong for the reason in the error message; it might have worked with CL = TRUE. The second option does not include a sex (group) effect in the model - use 'g' for this as in fit2 above (I admit the code should behave better, and I'll look at that). Your third option is wrong for the reason in the error message: groups are not used in CL = TRUE models (though they may be defined post hoc in derived.secr).

Murray

parts:
Hi Sam,

Are these mask covariates?  I'm thinking that the fitting function is looking for this covariates in the mask and not finding them?

For session covs, from the multi-session vignette:
"Other variation among sessions may be modelled with session-specific covariates. These are provided to secr.fit on-the-fly in the argument ‘sessioncov’ (they cannot be embedded in the capthist object like detector or individual covariates). The value for ‘sessioncov’ should be a dataframe with one row per session. Each column is a potential predictor in a model formula; other columns are ignored."

Can't model variation in density using trap covariates  if that what these relative abundance indices correspond to. Density is a point process across the mask--maybe it varies spatially across the mask, or it changes across sessions, or both.

If CL=TRUE, you can't model variation in density at all. The point process is conditioned out of the likelihood--density is a derived parameter. 

Cheers,

John
